newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says not taking sides on island dispute.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says not taking sides on island dispute.

text.p: Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said Singapore sides with neither China nor Japan in a dispute over islands in the East China Sea, the Straits Times said on Monday.
In a report from China's Shandong province, which Lee is currently visiting, the newspaper quoted him as saying the dispute was a question of sovereignty and of territory between China and Japan.
"We, of course, hope this question will be resolved peacefully, in accordance with international law and the law of the sea," Lee was quoted as saying.
The Straits Times said Lee stressed Singapore did not side with China or Japan, or with Taiwan which also claims sovereignty over the islands, called the Diaoyus by China and the Senkakus by Japan.

Noting there had been anti-Japanese protests in Taiwan and Hong Kong over the issue but not in China, Lee said: "I see China taking a cautious attitude. They also understand that their economic relations with Japan are important. They hope that Japan will continue to invest in China."
Lee Hsien Loong's father, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew, had earlier praised China for showing restraint in the dispute.
Japan has claimed the islands since 1895 while Chinese claims are centuries old.

The dispute flared anew in July when Japanese right-wingers erected a crude lighthouse on one of the islands to underscore Tokyo's claim. Hong Kong and Taiwan activists responded with a brief joint landing on the islands last week.
An earlier landing attempt resulted in the drowning of a Hong Kong activist.
